A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the meeting of revolutionary roads was the result of the convergence of a number of global and domestic factors, including the Cuban Revolution and the rise of a new internationalism; the Cold War, the Cuban missile crisis, and the Sino-Soviet split; the decline of the Alliance for Progress; the rise of the New Left and the New International Economic Order; and the emergence of a new generation of leaders in Chile.

the meeting of revolutionary roads in Chile and Cuba was the result of a process of convergence and rapprochement between the two countries that had begun during the early 1960s and that would continue after Allende's election in 1970.
we have tried to show that the meeting of the revolutionary roads was not the product of a single event, but of the complex interplay of global and domestic transformations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the meeting of revolutionary roads was the result of a long process that began with the Cuban revolution, and it is only through a careful examination of the complex interactions between the Chilean and Cuban revolutions that one can grasp the significance of this meeting.
